column3: requirement
Only struct and enum are nominal product and sum declaration spellings.
Callable result and empty-effect omission spellings preserve one semantic signature.
Lifetime syntax, higher-ranked regions, reborrowing, and variance obey Rust-style rules.
Each type has one principal Use interval and manual implementations may only restrict it.
Positive-lower obligations propagate through whole moves and deconstruction while discarded subtrees require zero use.
Drop is an orthogonal zero-use hook and is unavailable to positive-lower types.
Every named function and closure has a fresh compiler-generated callable identity.
Fn and RunsIn evidence is compiler-generated, sealed, and tied to the callable environment.
A capture-free callable uses the canonical empty environment ().
Shared environments remain open across arbitrary source-defined selector constraints until sealed.
Owned, shared, and unique environment access is represented by ordinary E, &E, and &mut E ownership.
Callable environment access has no separate receiver-mode semantic enum.
Available<E> is the sole erased incremental-alternative witness and zero-use release requires proof.
Static label brands are generative proof identities distinct from runtime leave targets.
Label-generic effects retain proof-only label identity and cannot be intercepted across brands.
Deep handlers, terminal operations, finite resumption quantities, replay, and cancellation compose.
The surface is test lowers through the shared pattern compiler with branch-scoped refinement evidence.
Control vocabulary such as if, loop, return, yield, await, and fail is ordinary source binding vocabulary.
Typed Core has no compiler-known control or arithmetic semantic nodes.
Standard control abstractions compile from ordinary declarations, fixities, callables, effects, and handlers.
An independent Core evaluator and the verified VM agree on executable semantics.
Structured diagnostics explain source labels and environments without exposing internal brand IDs.
Source code cannot manually implement Label, Environment, Fn, or RunsIn.
Source code cannot forge label, environment, refinement, or Available<E> evidence.
An exact-linear callable or environment cannot be activated twice on one control path.
Every owned value use remains inside its principal quantitative interval.
A label- or environment-dependent value cannot escape its generative lifetime.
A positive refinement binder is unavailable in a negative branch.
A protecting borrow prevents invalidation of its live refinement evidence.
Incompatible normal post-environments cannot join silently.
A custom Drop hook executes at most once on each legal normal or nonlocal cleanup path.
Safe code cannot partially move or ownership-deconstruct a custom-Drop aggregate.
Drop::drop cannot expose effects, suspension, or label transfer.
A one-shot continuation cannot be resumed twice.
Cancellation and cleanup cannot discard a captured must-move obligation.
A multi-shot continuation cannot duplicate a nonduplicable or uniquely borrowed capture.
An active label cannot cross a multi-shot continuation capture.
A label-generic effect cannot be intercepted using the wrong label brand.
A static label brand is never accepted as a forgeable runtime address or contradictory destination.
A closed executable cannot finish with an unhandled outward effect.
Sequential activation of one exact-linear environment is rejected.
Unequal branch post-state is rejected rather than repaired by implicit destruction.
Illegal implicit destruction of a positive-lower value is rejected.
An effectful destructor is rejected.
A closure or handler depending on an expired label is rejected.
A positive pattern binder used in a negative context is rejected.
Ordinary construction of an Available<E> witness is rejected.
A multi-shot resumption capturing a unique borrow is rejected.
